# iliad-087 — new formula and epithet renderings (14.109–221)

Rows in the format of the conventions table (Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose).

| πολυπίδακος (Ἴδης, 14.157; πίδαξ "spring") | "many-springed" | "many-springed" | "many-fountained", "of many streams", "well-watered"; a stock epithet of Ida and likely to recur |
| τὴν δὲ δολοφρονέουσα προσηύδα πότνια Ἥρη (14.197, whole-line speech introduction) | "And to her, with guile in her mind, spoke lady Hera:" | "Then lady Hera, with guile in her mind, spoke to her:" | "cunningly", "deceitfully", "with crafty thoughts"; follows the table's δολοφρονέουσα "with guile in your mind" (3.405) and the Odyssey's whole-line δολοφρονέων … "with guile in his mind"; προσηύδα "spoke to" as in ἔπεα πτερόεντα προσηύδα |
| τὴν δ’ ἠμείβετ’ ἔπειτα Διὸς θυγάτηρ Ἀφροδίτη (14.193, whole-line reply-formula) | "Her then answered the daughter of Zeus, Aphrodite:" | "Then Aphrodite, the daughter of Zeus, answered her:" | "Zeus’s daughter"; follows the table's τὴν δ’ ἠμείβετ’ ἔπειτα … rows and Διὸς θυγάτηρ "the daughter of Zeus" |

Uses of existing table rows without change: βοὴν ἀγαθός "good at the war-cry", ἄναξ ἀνδρῶν Ἀγαμέμνων "lord of men", κρείων ἐνοσίχθων "the lord earth-shaker", χρυσόθρονος Ἥρη "golden-throned", δῖα θεάων "heavenly even among goddesses", φιλότης "love", ἵμερος "longing", φίλον τέκος "dear child", αἰδοίη "revered", μάκαρες θεοί "blessed gods", ἀπήμονα … λιαρόν "harmless and warm", ἀλείψατο λίπ’ ἐλαίῳ "anointed richly with oil", ποιπνύοντα "bustling", κυδιάνειραν "man-glorifying", ἀνάλκιδα "without might", κοτεσσαμένη "bearing a grudge", ἀρήγω "help", οὐτάμενοι "wounded", ἄριστος "best", δαμνᾷ "subdue", πολυφόρβου "much-nourishing", ἀτιτάλλω "fostered", βῆ δ’ ἴμεν "set out to go", βὰν δ’ ἴμεν "set out to go", χόλος "anger", κότος "resentment", ἀρετή "excellence", ἔξοχος "standing out", ἀφνειός "rich", ὄρχατος "orchard", πυροφόρος "wheat-bearing", αὐτοκασίγνητος "own brother", ἔπος τ’ ἔφατ’ ἔκ τ’ ὀνόμαζε "spoke a word and called her by name" / "spoke, calling her by name".

Departures from published English (all in pronoun, punctuation or quotation marks only):
- 14.109 and 14.133: whole-unit repeats take the published `l` and `i` exactly. The Greek of 14.133 ends with an ano teleia here where the published unit ends with a full stop; the English is unchanged.
- 14.138 καί μιν φωνήσας ἔπεα πτερόεντα προσηύδα: the published English has "to her"; μιν is Agamemnon here, so "to him", as at 4.312 and 4.369.
- 14.148–149: the published wording of the two lines, in a sentence that runs on to ἧκεν; the `i` begins with a capital.
- 14.152 Ἀχαιοῖσιν δὲ μέγα σθένος ἔμβαλ’ ἑκάστῳ κτλ: the published subject is "she" (the earlier speaker is a goddess), here "he" (Poseidon); the Greek has a comma after καρδίῃ that the published unit lacks.
- 14.161 ἥδε δέ οἱ … βουλή: "him … his" of the published line becomes "her … her"; the rest of the published sentence (Nestor) is not in this unit.
- 14.186 ποσσὶ δ’ ὑπὸ λιπαροῖσιν ἐδήσατο καλὰ πέδιλα: the published line is the first of a longer unit about a man; "his" becomes "her", and the unit ends with a full stop here.
- 14.196 τελέσαι δέ με θυμὸς ἄνωγεν κτλ (= the Odyssey lines shipped in odyssey-022): the Odyssey’s English, with the closing quotation mark added because this is the last unit of Aphrodite’s speech.
- 14.212 οὐκ ἔστ’ οὐδὲ ἔοικε τεὸν ἔπος ἀρνήσασθαι (= the Odyssey line shipped in odyssey-036): the Odyssey’s English, with the closing quotation mark replaced by a semicolon because the speech goes on to line 213.
